newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LONDONERS AIM TO SHRUG OFF LEAGUE LETHARGY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LONDONERS AIM TO SHRUG OFF LEAGUE LETHARGY.

text.p: Chelsea and Wimbledon enter Sunday's F.A. Cup semifinal with their league form in tatters and their chances of qualifying for Europe fading fast.
In addition, Chelsea have been settling a few old scores in the dressing-room in the run-up to the most important match of their season.
But both sides know victory in Sunday's high noon clash in neutral North London will take them to within one match of a major trophy and a cherished place in Europe next season.
Chelsea have lost their last three premier league matches. Their most recent defeats were 3-0 at home to Arsenal and 3-1 away at relegation-threatened Coventry.
"I'm not happy, put it that way," said captain Dennis Wise, who was suspended for both matches but will return on Sunday.
"We're disappointed at letting in six goals in two games and only scoring once. We've got to be disappointed.
"We've done okay (this season) but we can do better, it's not quite good enough because our main ambition was to qualify for Europe."
Chelsea's Scotland defender Steve Clarke said the players' frustration came to a head after they conceded three goals in 10 minutes at Coventry in midweek.

"We got a bit carried away in the dressing-room and a few things were said," he revealed. "We're going into the semifinal on a bad run. With the players we've got, the performances have not been good enough."
The same could be said of Wimbledon, who have not won in their last eight league matches.
They lost 2-0 at home to Aston Villa on Wednesday and now have little chance of qualifying for Europe through the league.
But their cup form this season has been outstanding. They made the semifinals of both domestic competitions and knocked Manchester United out of the F.A. Cup.
They will also take solace from the choice of venue for Sunday's tie.
Wimbledon have not lost at Arsenal's Highbury in the league since their F.A. Cup-winning season of 1988. Their last victory in the league, way back on February 23, was at Arsenal.
Chelsea have injury doubts over Clarke, Welsh striker Mark Hughes and Romanian wing-back Dan Petrescu.
Wimbledon's talismanic captain Vinnie Jones is trying to shake off a shouder injury while midfielders Oyvind Leonhardson and Robbie Earle have hamstring strains.
The two sides have met only twice in the F.A. Cup -- in last year's sixth round, when they drew 2-2, and in the subsequent replay, which Chelsea won 3-1.
Wimbledon won 4-2 at Stamford Bridge in the league earlier this season and have generally had the better of their clashes in the decade since they won promotion to the premier league.
The winners of Sunday's match will face either Middlesbrough or outsiders Chesterfield in the final at Wembley on May 17.

Middlesbrough are still chasing a cup double, having made the final of the League Cup, while Chesterfield are bidding to become the first side from the third tier of English football to appear in the F.A. Cup final.
The two sides meet at Old Trafford in Manchester on Sunday afternoon, three hours after the all-London tie.
